hough.bandsTip: Number of bands (the strongest peaks of the Radon transform) taken from each pattern and used in triplet voting. More bands help weak or multi-phase patterns but add false bands and time. Orienta's default is 12; PyEBSDIndex itself defaults to 9.
hough.tSigmaTip: Smoothing along theta (the angle of a band) in the Radon transform: the sigma of a Gaussian, in Radon bins (1 bin = 1 degree). Larger values suppress noise but merge bands that lie at similar angles. Orienta's default is 2; PyEBSDIndex itself defaults to 1.
hough.rSigmaTip: Width of the band detector along rho (across a band): the sigma of a Gaussian second-derivative kernel, in Radon bins (1 bin is about 1/180 of the shorter pattern side). Set it near the apparent band width: larger finds wide bands and ignores narrow lines and noise, smaller resolves narrow bands. Orienta's default is 2; PyEBSDIndex itself defaults to 1.2.

matchesDialog.title: Dictionary Indexing — Pattern Match Quality
matchesDialog.clickHint: Click a pixel in the NCC map to inspect that pattern match.
matchesDialog.orientationHoughTip: For this phase the orientation was taken from Hough band-geometry indexing, because the spherical SO(3) correlation cannot tell apart two pseudo-symmetric variants with nearly identical patterns (today only point group -43m, e.g. Mg17Al12; results indexed before 22 September 2026 did this for m-3 and mmm as well). The score map (CI) is still from spherical.

The per-pixel counts are in the run's provenance note.
matchesDialog.tryVariantsTip: If the simulated pattern doesn't match, show candidate orientations (current + crystallographic pseudo-variants + Hough), each rendered with its match score. Pick the one that matches and apply it to the whole grain. Works for any phase.
matchesDialog.variantsHint: Pick the variant whose simulated pattern matches the experimental one ({{pg}}). R = render match (higher = better). Then apply it to the grain.
matchesDialog.applyGrainTip: Flood-fill the grain (connected, same phase) and flip every pixel to ITS own matching variant — intra-grain distortions are preserved and variant-split grains are fixed in one apply.

matchesDialog.suspicionHint: This match looks wrong — try the pseudo-symmetry variants.
matchesDialog.refineTip: After the flip, polish each pixel's orientation with a guarded Newton refinement. It is automatically discarded if a render-match spot check shows no improvement.

matchesDialog.applyAllTip: Fix the clicked grain AND every other grain map-wide with the same phase and the same wrong orientation. Each sibling is adopted only if its own render-NCC clearly improves — genuinely different small grains stay untouched. One Undo restores everything.

hoverTips.reflectorCount:
How many reflector families this phase contributes to the Hough band-triplet library.

Hough builds that library once per run and sizes it from the family count; it grows roughly with the CUBE of the number of distinct inter-pole angles. The same 70 families therefore cost a few MiB for a cubic phase and tens of GiB for a phase whose CIF carries no symmetry - and on Windows the memory is claimed the moment it is asked for, so an impossible request can take the machine down. Orienta refuses what does not fit rather than attempting it.

Fewer families is NOT free. Measured on Ni (58 families, 800 real patterns): 40 and 32 give exactly the same orientations as the full set; 24 indexes only 192 of 800 pixels and is 119.7 deg off; 16 fails completely - quietly, returning orientations that still look plausible. That is why this is your choice and not an automatic one. After lowering it, compare the indexed map against a run with more families before you rely on it.

Indexing reads only n_bands bands per pattern (12 by default), so the weakest families are rarely decisive - but rarely is not never, which is what the numbers above show.

This count is in ROWS of the reflector list: every symmetry equivalent and both signs of a reflector is one row, so a few families can already be dozens of rows (aluminium: 64 rows are 6 families; the first 24 rows leave out {111}). Use 'Reflector families' above for exact control by family. The row count is only used for a phase without a family selection of its own, and mainly protects memory.
hoverTips.reflectorNoSymmetry: The CIF is stored in space group P 1: every atom listed, no symmetry recorded. PyEBSDIndex then treats each reflector family as a single pole, so the number of distinct inter-pole angles - and with it the band-triplet library - explodes. Re-exporting the phase in its real space group makes this small and is the better fix; lowering the reflector count here is the workaround.

reflectorFamilies.title: Reflector families
reflectorFamilies.toggleTip: Which crystal planes (reflector families) Hough indexing matches the detected bands against for this phase. Open to see them, leave some out or add others. A phase without a selection of its own uses the default list.
reflectorFamilies.loading: Computing the reflector families (large unit cells take a while)...
reflectorFamilies.unavailable: Reflector families are not available for this file.
reflectorFamilies.intro: Hough indexing compares the detected bands with the angles between the planes listed here. Untick a family to leave it out or add one. A family whose pole is a multiple of an earlier one (for example {400} after {200}) is listed but ignored by PyEBSDIndex.
reflectorFamilies.tipColUse: Tick to use this family in Hough indexing.
reflectorFamilies.tipColFamily: Plane family {hkl}, written with the indices of one member; for hexagonal and trigonal phases with four indices {hkil}.
reflectorFamilies.tipColF: Kinematical structure factor |F| relative to the strongest family. Stronger families give stronger bands.
reflectorFamilies.tipColMult: Number of symmetry-equivalent planes in the family (both signs counted).
reflectorFamilies.tipTopN: Use only the N strongest families (by structure factor), skipping those that repeat the pole of a stronger one. Hough indexing needs at least two.
reflectorFamilies.tipAdd: Add a family that is not in the list, for example a weak or fine one. It is checked against the crystal first: forbidden reflections are refused.
reflectorFamilies.tipReset: Go back to the default list for this phase (d >= 1 Angstrom, |F| above 10 % of the strongest, at most 70 rows).
reflectorFamilies.tipRuleMinD: Smallest lattice plane spacing (Angstrom) considered when the list is built. Lower values add finer, weaker bands. Default 1.0.
reflectorFamilies.tipRuleF: Keep families whose kinematical structure factor is above this fraction of the strongest one. Default 0.1.
reflectorFamilies.tipRuleApply: Build the list again with these two numbers (still capped at 70 rows).
reflectorFamilies.costTooBig: does not fit the memory free now
reflectorFamilies.tipCost: Memory the band-triplet library of this selection needs. It grows quickly with the number of families.
reflectorFamilies.stale: This selection was made for a different crystal (another space group or cell) and is not applied. Reset it to the default.
reflectorFamilies.rowLimitNote: The row count below counts reflector rows, not families, and is not used while this phase has its own family selection.
reflectorFamilies.addedParallel: Added {{label}}. It has the same pole as {{other}}; PyEBSDIndex uses only the first of the two.
